Empirical Research Plan:  The Causal Effect of Attending Oversubscribed Schools in Denver’s Unified Enrollment System
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Identification Strategy  
   Identification method:  School-specific, priority-specific fuzzy Regression Discontinuity Design (FRD), implemented as an instrumental-variables (2SLS) estimator that instruments actual enrollment with an indicator for “winning” the random tie-breaking lottery at each school’s cut-off.  
   Justification:  
   • Within every (school × grade × year × priority) cell, seats are allocated in descending order of a uniformly–random lottery number; conditional on an applicant’s submitted rank list and priority status, the lottery number is the only remaining source of variation in whether the student receives an offer.  
   • The running variable (lottery number) is as-good-as randomly assigned, permitting local comparisons of students just above vs. just below the last seat offered (the cut-off).  
   • Oversubscription generates fuzzy, not sharp, discontinuities because some winners decline and some losers later enroll via wait-list moves. Hence a 2SLS/Fuzzy RD is appropriate.  

2. Treatment and Control  
   • Treatment variable (Dᵢ):  An indicator that student i actually enrolls in the focal school (or sector, e.g., any charter).  
   • Instrument (Zᵢ):  Lottery-winner indicator equal to 1 if the student’s lottery number is above the seat-cutoff in her (school × priority × grade × year) risk set; 0 otherwise.  
   • Control group:  Students with the same submitted preference list and priority status who just miss the lottery cut-off (Zᵢ=0).  
   • Event date / timing:  Outcomes (standardized math & reading test scores) are measured after one year of attendance (end-of-grade 6 or 9).  
   • Running variable:  Lottery score (uniform[0,1]); Cut-off: the worst score that received an offer within each risk set.  

3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
   A1. Random assignment of lottery numbers: conditional on preference list & priority, numbers are i.i.d. uniform and independent of potential outcomes. Plausible because numbers are computer-generated and revealed after lists lock.  
   A2. Continuity of potential outcomes at the cut-off: in the absence of winning, achievement would evolve smoothly in lottery number. Reasonable given the random tie-break and no reason for sharp jumps in unobservables.  
   A3. No manipulation of the running variable: families cannot influence their lottery number. Plausible (numbers assigned centrally).  
   A4. Exclusion restriction: winning affects outcomes only through attending the focal school (no other channels such as information or expectations). Reasonable, though we will test for changes in peer composition and subsequent school choice to gauge indirect channels.  
   A5. Monotonicity: winning weakly increases probability of enrolling in the school (no defiers). Highly plausible—being offered a seat never makes enrollment less likely.  

4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation  
   T1. Strategic preference submission creates endogenous risk sets.  Mitigation: condition on the entire submitted rank list; estimate within students who rank the focal school first; additionally control for list length & other rank positions.  
   T2. Post-lottery wait-list moves blur treatment/control purity.  Mitigation: treat enrollment as the endogenous treatment and rely on 2SLS; calculate reduced-form effects as robustness; report complier characteristics.  
   T3. Spillovers to control students (crowd-out to lower-ranked schools).  Mitigation: cluster standard errors at school-risk-set level; estimate sector-level effects (charter vs. TPS) where crowd-out may be less of a concern; explore MTO-style bounding exercises.  

5. R Code Outline  

```r
#----------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # fast IV & FE regressions
library(rdrobust)    # bandwidth & RD inference
#----------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load and merge data
apps <- fread("dps_applications.csv")   # one row per application
scores <- fread("dps_testscores.csv")   # end-of-year scores
dt <- merge(apps, scores, 
            by = c("student_id","year","grade"), all.x = TRUE)

#----------------------------------------------------
# 2. Construct key variables
# a) within each school–priority–grade–year risk set, find cut-off lottery number
dt[, cutoff := max(lottery_number[offer==1]), 
        by = .(school_id, priority, year, grade)]

# b) instrument: win (1=yes)
dt[, win := as.integer(lottery_number <= cutoff)]

# c) endogenous treatment: enroll in focal school
dt[, enroll := as.integer(enrolled_school_id == school_id)]

# d) outcome: standardized z-score (mean 0, sd 1 by grade×year statewide)
dt[, z_math := (math_scale - mean(math_scale, na.rm=TRUE)) / 
                 sd(math_scale, na.rm=TRUE), by = .(grade, year)]
                 
# restrict to applicants who ranked the focal school 1st
dt1 <- dt[rank_in_list == 1]

# optional: impose common support |lottery - cutoff| <= h
h <- 0.10         # bandwidth
dt1 <- dt1[abs(lottery_number - cutoff) <= h]

#----------------------------------------------------
# 3. Main FRD / IV specification
# School fixed effects to pool across schools
iv_fit <- feols(z_math ~ 1 | school_id, data = dt1,
                iv = ~ enroll | win, cluster = ~school_id)

summary(iv_fit)

#----------------------------------------------------
# 4. Robustness:  rdrobust within each large school, aggregate
rd_res <- rdrobust(y = dt1$z_math, x = dt1$lottery_number - dt1$cutoff,
                   c = 0, fuzzy = dt1$enroll)

print(rd_res)

#----------------------------------------------------
```

6. Expected Results  
Prior:  Oversubscribed charter schools will raise math and reading scores by roughly 0.10–0.25 standard deviations after one year, consistent with prior urban charter evidence; oversubscribed district magnet schools may show smaller or zero average gains once selection is removed.  

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (FRD)  
C1. Continuity of baseline covariates at cut-off ………………… 1  
C2. No sorting/manipulation of running variable ………………… 1  
C3. Relevance of first stage (π ≠ 0) ……………………………………… 1  
C4. Exclusion restriction / single channel …………………………… 0.5  
C5. Local estimate generalizes only to compliers (LATE) ……… 0.5  

Total ≈ 4/5.  The key remaining concerns are potential indirect channels (C4) and external validity (C5), which will be discussed and probed in the paper.
